schools.name: East Lansing

state_titles.notes: Team inducted into Greater Lansing Area Sports Hall of Fame (team list).

Final played March 15, 2025 at Breslin Center. Cameron Hutson 20 pts; Kingston Thomas 19 pts, 12 reb; Kelvin (KJ) Torbert 16. First title since 1958. Semifinal: beat defending champ Orchard Lake St. Mary's 51-44 (Mar 14, 2025).

state_runner_ups.notes: MHSAA list does not name runner-up coaches.
Final March 14, 2026 at Breslin. KJ Torbert 28 pts in final game. Semifinal: beat Bloomfield Hills Brother Rice 55-52 on Torbert 3 with 1.2 sec left (Mar 13, 2026).

schools.final_fours_note: Derived from Finals appearances (reached Final => reached Semifinal stage). No additional semifinal-only appearances were verified; a complete MHSAA semifinal list for East Lansing was not found.

notable_players.name: Jim Hornberger
notable_players.accolades: All-state in football, basketball and baseball; basketball All-City 1962 and 1963; Dell Magazine All-American 1963; first inductee of East Lansing HS Hall of Fame; Greater Lansing Area Sports HOF 1992

notable_players.name: Ben Poquette
notable_players.grad_year: 1973 (inferred from senior honors; not explicitly stated)
notable_players.accolades: All-City 1973, team captain and MVP; Greater Lansing Area Sports HOF 1990
notable_players.college: Central Michigan (1974-77; First Team All-MAC 1977; CMU Athletics HOF 1987)
notable_players.pro: NBA: Detroit Pistons, Utah Jazz, Cleveland Cavaliers, Chicago Bulls (1977-87); described as Greater Lansing's first NBA player

notable_players.name: Thomas (T.J.) Jackson
notable_players.grad_year: 1998 (inferred from his 1998 start at Butler; not explicitly stated)
notable_players.accolades: Point guard (5-foot-9), born in East Lansing. At Butler became the school's all-time leader in assists and steals and its only player with 1,000 points and 500 assists; led Butler in assists four straight seasons, two-time first-team All-Horizon League, two-time Horizon League All-Defensive Team. Butler won 95 games in his four years with two NCAA Tournament trips. Named to Butler's Team of the Sesquicentennial; Butler Athletics Hall of Fame.
notable_players.pro: Undrafted in 2002. Played 2003-15 in Sweden (Sallén, Uppsala; 2007 Basketligan All-Star), the Netherlands (Den Helder; ZZ Leiden, 2011 Dutch league champion, 2012 NBB Cup and Supercup, 2012 DBL All-Star) and Germany (BBC Bayreuth, 2010 Pro A champion). Later an assistant coach in the G League (Erie, Maine, Northern Arizona, Salt Lake City) and at Evansville.

notable_players.name: Paul Stoll
notable_players.pro: Long pro career (Mexico LNBP titles 2020, 2021; Israeli League title 2013 with Maccabi Haifa); Mexico national team, 2013 FIBA Americas gold

notable_players.name: Brandon Johns Jr.
notable_players.accolades: AP Class A Player of the Year 2017; AP first team all-state 2016, 2017, 2018; Detroit Free Press Dream Team 2018; Detroit News Dream Team 2017, 2018; LSJ Player of the Year 2016, 2017; BCAM Best of the Best 2018; Mr. Basketball runner-up (2nd in voting); ESPN Top 100 (No. 60)

notable_players.name: Cameron Hutson
notable_players.accolades: AP D1 first-team all-state (2024, 2025); LSJ co-Player of the Year 2024; led all scorers (20) in 2025 D1 Final; son of former MSU player Andre Hutson

notable_players.name: Kelvin (KJ) Torbert, Jr.
notable_players.accolades: Michigan Mr. Basketball 2026 (first son of a former winner; father Kelvin Torbert, 2001, Flint Northwestern); Michigan Sports Writers D1 Player of the Year 2026; AP D1 first-team all-state 2024; 2025 D1 state champion; 2026 D1 runner-up

notable_players.name: Kingston Thomas
notable_players.accolades: 19 pts, 12 reb in 2025 D1 Final win; Michigan Sports Writers D1 all-state second team 2026

notable_coaches.name: Gus Ganakas
notable_coaches.notes: Coached 1958 Class B state champions (undefeated). Later Michigan State head coach 1969-76 (89-84). Died Jan. 11, 2019.

notable_coaches.name: Steve Finamore
notable_coaches.notes: 128-44 record; two straight CAAC Blue titles; coached Brandon Johns (team 24-1 in 2017, 23-1 in 2016; 2018 regional title, state quarterfinal).

notable_coaches.name: Ray Mitchell
notable_coaches.years: 2018-19 to present (took over seven seasons before 2025 title)
notable_coaches.notes: East Lansing graduate. 2025 Division 1 state champion (28-1); 2026 Division 1 runner-up (27-2); three quarterfinal trips in the four years before 2025.

notes: Wikipedia pages were fetched via WebFetch; Mr. Basketball list cross-checked for KJ Torbert by WILX and AP stories.

No Hal Schram Mr. Basketball winners from Lansing Everett, Sexton, Okemos, Holt, Grand Ledge, DeWitt, Haslett, Mason, St. Johns or Lansing Catholic were found in the 1981-2026 list. Brandon Johns (East Lansing, 2018) finished 2nd; Johnathon Jones (Okemos, 2006) finished 4th.
Bryn Forbes (NBA champion) attended Lansing Sexton (per 97.5 NOW), not East Lansing.
No comprehensive LSJ Player of the Year list was found; only scattered years are included.

CAAC divisions (2025-26): Blue = DeWitt, East Lansing, Everett, Grand Ledge, Holt, Okemos, Waverly; Red = Eastern, Haslett, Mason, Fowlerville, St. Johns, Williamston; White = Lansing Catholic, Sexton, and others. Source: https://caacsports.org/?p=39
